---
title: Build a plugin
description: Pick between a PLUGIN.md document, a remote (MCP) plugin and a bundled (SDK) plugin, set up the repositories, and get from your first tool to a marketplace listing.
icon: Hammer
---

A plugin connects PKU Harness to a campus service or adds a capability. The agent and the user
both go through the same typed tools, so most of the work is finding the service's API, wrapping
it in good tools, and adding a widget or screen where one helps.

## Choose the kind

| | Plugin document (`PLUGIN.md`) | Remote plugin | Bundled TypeScript plugin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Use for | Most campus integrations: campus or public requests plus extraction, with the user's campus session where needed | Your own service, anything heavy or needing general code | The harness's own features (dashboard, schedule, scheduler, memory, model providers…) and integrations the language can't express yet |
| Language | YAML steps + safe expressions, interpreted by the app | Any (MCP over Streamable HTTP) | TypeScript + zod + React Native |
| Release | `git push`; installed and updated by link | Deploy your server; no app release | Ships with app releases (open an issue first) |
| Start from | [Quickstart](/en/docs/build/quickstart), [Declarative plugins](/en/docs/build/declarative-plugins), or [write it with the AI](/en/docs/build/ai-authoring) | [`templates/remote-plugin`](/en/docs/build/remote-plugin) | [`definePlugin`](/en/docs/build/bundled-plugin) |

The official campus integrations classrooms, campus-events, grades, canteen, shuttle and notices
are plugin documents. The other integrations are still TypeScript and are being ported one by one.

## The path

<Steps>
<Step>

### Read the concepts

[Plugins](/en/docs/concepts/plugins), [Tools and effects](/en/docs/concepts/tools-and-effects),
[Permissions](/en/docs/concepts/permissions) and [Security](/en/docs/concepts/security) set the
rules every plugin follows.

</Step>
<Step>

### Find the protocol

If [`pkucli`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pkucli) already talks to the service, port it from there
and credit the file. See [Porting from pkucli](/en/docs/build/porting-from-pkucli).

</Step>
<Step>

### Write the tools

One tool per operation, honest effects, bounded inputs, and descriptions written for the model.
For a document, see [Declarative plugins](/en/docs/build/declarative-plugins); for code, see
[Tools and schemas](/en/docs/build/tools).

</Step>
<Step>

### Add UI

Documents can add generative-UI widgets and screens, Settings rows and slash commands. Bundled
plugins can also add native screens. See [UI contributions](/en/docs/build/ui) and
[Languages](/en/docs/build/i18n).

</Step>
<Step>

### Test

Documents use `bun run plugin validate|test` with recorded responses. TypeScript logic uses
`bun test`, the agent loop uses the mock model, and MCP uses the demo remote plugin. See
[Testing](/en/docs/build/testing).

</Step>
<Step>

### Publish

Share the install link and register in the marketplace. See [Publishing](/en/docs/build/publishing),
plus the marketplace's [manifest reference](/en/docs/marketplace/manifest) and
[submit flow](/en/docs/marketplace/publishing).

</Step>
</Steps>

## Repositories you need

| Repository | You need it for |
| --- | --- |
| [`pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins) | The SDK and plugin language, the author CLI (`bun run plugin`), the official documents and bundled plugins, the registry, the remote template and examples. Start here. |
| [`pkuinfo/pku-harness`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness) | The app, to run your bundled plugin on a device or emulator. Documents don't need it until you try campus requests live. |
| [`pkuinfo/pkucli`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pkucli) | Reference implementations of PKU service protocols (Rust). |

```bash
mkdir pku-info && cd pku-info
git clone https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins.git     # SDK, plugins, registry, template
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness.git   # only to run bundled plugins in the app
cd pku-harness-plugins && bun install && bun test
```

<Callout title="No npm packages">
  You use the SDK and plugins straight from the GitHub repository. Work inside a checkout of
  `pku-harness-plugins`: its bun workspace and `tsconfig.json` resolve `@pku-harness/sdk` to
  `packages/sdk/src`. The app pulls the same repository in as the git submodule `plugins/`.
  Remote plugins don't need the SDK at all.
</Callout>

## Ground rules (from CONTRIBUTING.md)

1. **Tools are the API.** Give each one a clear Chinese `title` (users see it) and a `description`
   written for the model that says when and how to use it. Validate input (`input` fields for
   documents, zod for bundled, JSON Schema for MCP).
2. **Declare effects honestly.** Read-only tools set `effect: read` (documents and bundled) or
   `readOnlyHint: true` (MCP). Anything that changes state, spends money or posts publicly must
   say so.
3. **Never ask for campus passwords.** Credentials stay on the user's phone.
4. **Return data, not instructions.** The model sees tool results as data.
5. **Declare what you reach.** In a document that's `campus`, `network` and `abilities`
   (`requires` is derived); in code it's `requires`. Don't depend on a shell or filesystem on the
   phone.
6. **Port campus protocols from pkucli** where it already implements them, and credit the source.
7. **Be bilingual.** A document has `i18n.en`. A bundled plugin needs an English overlay for every
   user-facing manifest string and a `src/strings.ts` table for screen and widget text.
